approach.method_basis: The Parent grows a persistent tree of molecular graph edits and buys the novel frontier molecules directly. Each accepted result updates only the path that generated it, retaining completed counts, pending counts, accumulated returns and the best observed return. Selection blends each eligible sibling's best return and visit density using molecular similarity. A strict accepted improvement replaces the active topology with two fresh ordered roots: the new incumbent and the incumbent from before that feedback batch, each initialized from its original scored receipt. The same shared selector currently governs competition between these roots and between deeper branches; raw visit counts govern widening.
approach.novelty: Remove statistical borrowing only between the two roots after an incumbent promotion. Each root will compete using its own observed peak and actual completed and pending counts, so evidence from the other origin cannot flatten their differences. This tests whether more distinct origin evidence restores useful refinement while retaining both origins. The supplied same-Parent sibling list is empty. Earlier branches tested adding the second origin or removing sharing deeper in a single-root tree; neither tested this post-promotion root consumer.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-b13ef5ae4ba8 loses useful refinement after expanding fresh-origin membership. Its complete Search mean is 0.4809700595412967 (SD 0.025313161830483537), down 0.018526255130948004 from its own Parent n-e4b751133c75. The preceding origin receives 1686/3580 post-promotion purchases and produces 47 global improvements, but useful current origins fall from 101/114 to 72/115; access is real while conversion is worse. Full and late global gain rates fall to 4.087169227484811/4350 and 0.8656010443094923/2175. The exact cause is not established. All 7430 observed post-promotion root rows have off-diagonal completed support and 6258 have off-diagonal pending support; an own-peak/own-count replay changes 389/3715 actual-state root choices in 12/15 cells and joins to 369 actual accepted purchases. These are alternative choices on purchased Parent states, without alternative rewards. The independent receipt join is recorded in policy/scratch/r0056-00-improve-L01/plan/audit-summary.json and its per-seed/task audits citing the underlying Parent logs and trajectories. n-3f6f7c11f468 separately lost 0.05230656961667265 when deeper sharing was removed on the single-root host, so it supports preserving that distinct consumer and does not settle this root question.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse search-policy-r56-support-and-statistical-consumers and its recorded queries; no new search was performed. Execute only the frozen internal-evidence root-consumer removal. The external alternatives remain deferred; this is not an implementation of RAVE, online multivalid prediction, a coherent mean-basis GP or a new regional model. Prospective exact-state own/shared receipts, paid-path joins and complete full/late conversion test the claim without treating exposure as benefit.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen review and the complete accepted Parent evidence support this exact conditional removal: dual-origin membership reached 1686 paid preceding-origin descendants yet reduced current useful roots to 72/115 and reduced complete mean by 0.018526255130948004. The source-checked own-root replay changes 389/3715 choices, with 369 accepted paths joined independently in this ticket audit. These observations justify testing dilution at the already implemented post-promotion joint root statistical consumer. They do not prove dilution caused the loss. The deeper-removal counterexample n-3f6f7c11f468 concerns a different boundary and single-root lifecycle, so deeper sharing remains unchanged.

sources.applicability: Context for interpreting direct versus shared statistics only. hypothesis: Condition-scoped removal of the joint off-diagonal value and completed/pending-density consumer at parent_id == 0 AND episode > 0 after a successful fresh dual-root promotion. For each eligible root use its own N,W,M,O: D=N, S=W, B=N*M for N>0 else 0, P=O, Qbest=M for N>0 else absent, exploitation=M for N>0 else the inherited neutral default. Use the inherited beta*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/(N+O)) bonus when N+O>0, zero-started priority otherwise, and earliest-occurrence ties. The own N includes its one original cached context and actual episode returns; these contexts are not new oracle observations. Removing cross-origin borrowing should restore differences in actual root evidence, change competing root selections and their paid descendants, and improve current-origin and total full/late refinement. Value and density are removed together as one existing consumer; no separate mediator attribution is claimed.

finding_summary.headline: Independent root statistics improved full and late gains, but the method still trails the formal Anchor
finding_summary.insights:
This isolates a conditional cost of statistical borrowing between the two promoted origins. At the registered descriptive 0.002 scale, removing that joint value-and-density consumer improves the complete mean, supporting negative contribution of the removed consumer in this composition. It does not establish that sharing is generally harmful, separate value from visit-density effects, or revise the earlier finding about adding a second origin. Nor is the result explained by giving the current origin more turns: every changed same-state decision selected the preceding origin, and current-origin purchases actually fell from 1,894 to 1,891 while preceding-origin purchases rose from 1,686 to 1,689. The current-origin benefit therefore reflects changed adaptive paths and returns, not a demonstrated matched-root causal mediator.

The aggregate gain is uneven. Two task/seed cells provide +0.51657 of endpoint-sum improvement; the remaining thirteen together lose 0.00518. Full incumbent gain is another expression of final endpoints, not independent evidence. Late gain also needs a timing qualification: one docking session supplies 62.67% of the net late-gain increase after reaching only 0.35094 at the midpoint versus the Parent’s 0.98189, then finishes slightly worse. Both registered rates improve, but this does not establish uniformly faster refinement.

The method still generates broad scaffold variation without consistently retaining productive molecular structure. Of 2,175 late purchases, 182 have fewer than six heavy atoms and 141 exceed fifty, compared with 170 and 141 in the Parent. The molecular assessment finds useful amine–aryl and carbonyl-containing arrangements among stronger products, alongside fragmentation, oversized graphs, unusual heteroatom bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. This supports a proposal-operator limitation: feedback-conditioned graph edits that preserve useful local arrangements and coherent molecular size are a missing capability to investigate. These records do not establish scaffold collapse or prove that a new operator will improve scores. The outcome settles the registered root-consumer contrast on this Search panel; separate mediators, wider transfer and the broader tree approach remain open.
finding_summary.results: The removal operated within its intended boundary. Own-root statistics differed from shared statistics in all 7,498 eligible rows, changed 374 of 3,749 root decisions in twelve of fifteen sessions, and reached 358 accepted descendants, including 228 late purchases. The initial forest, deeper sharing, two-root membership and exact receipt accounting passed reconstruction. Across all 4,350 paid optimizer observations, incumbent gain per purchase rose from 0.00093958 to 0.00105714. Over late ordinals 146–290 it rose from 0.00039798 to 0.00085398. Current origins producing any global improvement rose from 72/115 (62.61%) to 78/120 (65.00%), and their total gain increased from 1.64282 to 2.65066. All fifteen sessions completed. Mean final score rose from 0.480970 to 0.515062, a paired gain of 0.034092; all three seed means improved, while six task/seed endpoints improved, six fell and three stayed identical. The formal Anchor remains higher at 0.607030: the Child trails by 0.091968 and misses the separate Anchor +0.002 score target. Thus activation and the preregistered conversion prediction are confirmed, with the score-target falsifier separately triggered.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, chemically varied products retain useful amine–aryl motifs but also fragments, oversized graphs and unusual heteroatom bonds.
molecular.overall_character: The complete Child and published code Parent n-b13ef5ae4ba8 Search panels were read: all five objectives, seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted observations per cell including ten initial records, hence 4350 optimizer molecules per node. The frozen comparison separately marks child_complete=true and paired_complete=true; no task trajectory or Parent pairing is missing. These accepted trajectories do not enumerate rejected invalid or duplicate suggestions. The generated chemistry includes fused aromatic heterocycles, amides and imides, ethers, esters, basic saturated amine rings, halogenated aryl groups, unsaturated linkers, and densely bridged N/O cages. Rings and aromatic systems are abundant, not missing: the digest ring-closure rates range from 0.8690 to 0.9379 and aromatic-text rates from 0.5908 to 0.8977; these are molecule-level text indicators, not aromatic-atom fractions. RDKit perception finds rings in 3929/4350 and aromatic rings in 3435/4350 Child optimizer records. Broad graph variation coexists with repeated high-score series within individual sessions; unique scaffolds alone do not establish useful chemical exploration. Full Child heavy-atom tails are 321/4350 below six and 239/4350 above fifty, versus Parent 319/4350 and 244/4350. Late optimizer ordinals 146..290 contain 182/2175 and 141/2175 respectively, versus Parent 170/2175 and 141/2175. Thus both size tails remain present late. A conventional medicinal-chemistry subset is visible, but N–halogen, O–halogen, peroxide and complicated bridged products make overall synthetic plausibility questionable; these are structural assessments without route or stability experiments. All digest stereocentre and charged-text rates are zero. RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2476/4350 Child products; absence of written charge does not imply absence of protonatable amines. Full fragment-excluded consecutive-pair Morgan similarity is 0.232616 over 4014 within-session Child pairs versus 0.234098 over 4016 Parent pairs; late values are 0.239876/1978 and 0.243761/1990. The descriptor is radius-two, 2048-bit Morgan Tanimoto after retaining heavy-atom counts >=6 within each stream, with consecutive retained molecules paired; these are not all-pairs statistics, initial-set distances, or independent samples. Typed/generic scaffold counts and complete per-cell full/late denominators are recorded in policy/scratch/r0056-00-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json. Exact read-file provenance is policy/scratch/r0056-00-improve-L01/molecular/inputs-sha256.json: each Child snapshot is byte-identical to its original trusted staging trajectory, each Parent source is an existing published trajectory, and original paths and SHA256 hashes are preserved. The summary explicitly lists each per-cell audit, which cites both underlying files and their hashes. No future archive path is used as existing evidence. These are conditional chemical associations from this Search panel, not attribution to a component or an activation verdict.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer products centre on substituted indoles, ring-expanded pyrrole-containing systems and fused O/N heteroaromatics, with fluorophenyl or fluoropyridyl groups, amides or ketones, methoxy/methyl substituents and occasional aminomethyl groups. Median heavy-atom count is 24, with a 1..91 range; 809 have rings and 778 have aromatic rings. The best observed molecule is a 25-heavy-atom, three-aromatic-ring acetyl indole with an aryl O–N linkage and aminomethyl substitution. The surrounding amide/heteroaromatic chemistry is recognizable, whereas the O–N derivatives, ring expansions and large concatenated structures have less evident synthetic routes. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 428/301, versus Parent 417/285; these include low-scoring products.
liabilities: The full stream contains 54 products below six heavy atoms and 21 above fifty; the late stream still contains 33/435 and 11/435 respectively.
O–N-linked aryl products and peroxide-containing large ring systems complicate stability and route assessment; written validity is not a synthesis demonstration.
missing_features: Reliable retention of the compact heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangements seen among the better products is missing from many subsequent proposals; ring chemistry itself is plentiful.
The observed panel does not establish an unseen target-specific motif; chemically ordinary alternatives to the high-score O–N linkage remain an unresolved coverage question.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed 1 evaluation 264 scores 0.40497388700123543 for the acetyl/O–N-linked indole; its related dimethyl analogue at evaluation 115 scores 0.3940393921126993. A different ketone/anilide framework at evaluation 216 scores 0.4037744036160393, so no single O–N motif is established as necessary. The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. By contrast NF and O score 0, and a highly expanded multi-ring product at seed 0 evaluation 277 also scores 0. This supports retention of intermediate-sized heteroaromatic/carbonyl structures rather than indiscriminate shrinking or enlargement. Parent best scores by seeds 0/1/2 are 0.42762099872850584, 0.38277504802042894 and 0.3869228553267078; Child values are 0.3886780621304781, 0.40497388700123543 and 0.3869228553267078. Parent seed 0 retained a compact N-methyl indole carboxamide, whereas the Child seed 0 best has an expanded unsaturated ring; seed 2 has the same best fused heteroaromatic molecule. These differences do not identify a universally rewarded functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The products are mostly branched aromatic or heteroaromatic systems with ethers, ester/carbonyl groups, amidine or aminal-like linkers and fluorinated aryl substituents. Median size is 30 heavy atoms, range 1..108; 775/870 have rings and 726/870 aromatic rings. The best seed 0 series combines a substituted indole-like fused aromatic core, N-fluorination, a fluoroaminopyridyl amidine, methyl ester and an O–S–O appendage. Seed 1 also reaches a less fused aromatic/pyridyl aminal series; seed 2 reaches highly fused azaaromatic/lactone structures. The nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts are 363/269 versus Parent 420/321, despite substantial whole-panel variety. Ordinary substituents coexist with unusual bond environments, so structural complexity is not evidence of easy synthesis.
liabilities: The full stream has 79 products below six heavy atoms and 63 above fifty; late counts remain 45/435 and 37/435.
Direct N–halogen bonds occur in 91/870 products, including high-score N-fluorinated heterocycles; acyl fluoride and N-chloro variants also occur among high scores.
Peroxide fragments can share the 0.5 score floor with ordinary small molecules, so the floor does not certify chemically useful products.
missing_features: Reliable production of complete decorated aromatic frameworks is absent from the fragment-like tail that remains at the observed 0.5 floor.
The highest observed series does not demonstrate comparably rewarded, synthetically ordinary alternatives to its N–F and O–S–O environments; their necessity is unproven.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed 0 evaluation 282 scores 0.5981337568778717 for the heavily decorated N-fluorinated amidine. An analogue with conventional methoxy groups instead of the O–S–O appendage scores 0.5973295212604173 at evaluation 237. The initial aromatic imide scores 0.548381482770623; Cl, COOC and N-methylaniline all occur at 0.5. The observed increment accompanies organized, substituted aromatic frameworks, but the near-equal top analogues do not establish that the unusual appendage is beneficial. Parent best scores by seeds 0/1/2 are 0.5910556003223207, 0.5966919537370974 and 0.5888218535277359; Child values are 0.5981337568778717, 0.5945168486556299 and 0.5888218535277359. Parent seed 0 instead favours a fused amidine/azaaryl system, Parent seed 1 a sulfur-containing fused heteroaromatic aminal; seed 2 retains the same fused azaaromatic/lactone best molecule. This is varied high-score chemistry, not an identified unique missing scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: This panel most clearly produces conventional basic-amine/aryl combinations: N-substituted pyrrolidines or azetidines, halophenyl and methoxyphenyl groups, alkyl or alkenyl spacers, and occasional sulfoxide or secondary amine links. Median size is 30 heavy atoms, range 1..88; 816/870 products have rings and 729/870 aromatic rings. Seed 0 best is a 22-heavy-atom pyrrolidine–cyclohexyl–bromoaryl product; seed 1 best is a 31-heavy-atom azetidine/sulfoxide diaryl product; seed 2 best is a 28-heavy-atom biaryl/secondary-amine/N-methylpyrrolidine product. These are recognizable medicinal-chemistry fragments, although their assembly and stereochemistry are not demonstrated. Nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts are 445/326, versus Parent 414/299.
liabilities: The full stream contains 48 products below six heavy atoms and 55 above fifty; late counts are 25/435 and 27/435.
Large halogenated aryl/alkyl structures can be highly hydrophobic, and some high-scoring derivatives introduce acyl fluoride or O–F groups; solubility and stability are unmeasured.
Unspecified tetrahedral centres occur in 760/870 accepted products; no stereochemical assignments are supplied in the digest.
missing_features: Basic amine rings are already available; the missing consistency is preserving a free amine with an adequately sized aryl/cycloalkyl framework across weak proposals.

Defined stereochemical configurations are absent from the cited high-score products, including stereogenic saturated rings and the sulfoxide-bearing product; the trajectory does not establish a stereochemical score preference.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed 1 evaluation 245 scores 0.9861328849100068 for the azetidine/sulfoxide diaryl product; seed 2 evaluation 96 scores 0.971550831584605 for a secondary-amine-linked biaryl/N-methylpyrrolidine, and seed 0 evaluation 299 scores 0.9598069062933017 for the smaller pyrrolidine/cyclohexyl/aryl structure. In contrast the N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine carboxanilide at seed 1 evaluation 208 scores 0.00019488185027450726 and a small dichloroaryl sulfone scores 0.00032141189568530486. Free basic amine centres combined with hydrophobic ring frameworks are associated with the better results; an N-sulfonyl ring nitrogen is chemically different from a free amine. These are not controlled substitutions or a measured binding-mode explanation. Parent best scores by seeds 0/1/2 are 0.7348361230868937, 0.9955091591007366 and 0.9820177455680393; the Child has a smaller best seed 0 product but remains in similar amine/aryl families for seeds 1/2. per_task.generated_character: The leading series contains polycyclic aryl/azaheteroaromatic structures with cyclic imide-like carbonyl pairs, N-methyl groups, an aryl ether bridge and ethoxy or ester substitution. The whole stream has a median of 30 heavy atoms and a 1..107 range, with rings in 773/870 products and aromatic rings in 692/870. The best seed 2 product has 33 heavy atoms and five rings, three aromatic. Seed 0 explores larger sulfonamide/lactam structures but never exceeds the initial incumbent. Recognizable carbonyl and aromatic units coexist with unusual annulations and N/O-rich ring connectivity, making routes uncertain. Nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts are 395/309, versus Parent 391/307.

Some high-scoring seed 1 structures include O–F substitution and elaborate N/O ring patterns; the last seed 2 product contains a peroxide linkage.
Complex annulation and large coupled polycycles have no demonstrated synthetic route, even where local carbonyl groups are familiar.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the productive aryl/carbonyl/N framework is missing in low-score fragments and oversized combinations; adding rings alone does not fill the gap.
The available molecules do not reveal an absent target-specific group; the high-score region remains concentrated in closely related complex polycyclic carbonyl frameworks.

The initial aromatic imide scores 0.1678386594791329. Small S, NCOF, N#CCCN and C#N products score 0, and a much larger elaborated polycycle at seed 2 evaluation 297 scores only 0.10821830454839103. The observed gradient favours retention of a structured aryl/carbonyl/N framework over fragmentation or simple bulk addition. Parent best accepted scores by seeds 0/1/2 are 0.1678386594791329, 0.1933353363067749 and 0.2096115099737028; Child values are 0.1678386594791329, 0.1899312343197107 and 0.20504156174308186. per_task.generated_character: This panel favours unusually dense heteroatom cages rather than mainly planar aromatic products. Median size is 22 heavy atoms, range 1..77; 756/870 products have rings but only 510/870 have aromatic rings. Seed 0 best is a heteroaryl/phenyl pyrazoline-like thioamide with an aminomethyl side chain; seed 1 best is a fused nitrogen-rich polycycle with amino, halogen and vinyl-thiol substitution. Seed 2 best has 26 heavy atoms, three nonaromatic rings, dense C–F/C–Br substitution, an O–F bond, N–O cage connectivity, aminomethyl, hydroxyl and thiol groups. Consistent preservation of the favourable size/composition balance is absent, as a close late cage derivative and tiny final fragments lose nearly all observed score; the trajectories do not identify a missing target-specific pharmacophore.

A closely related more hydroxylated structure at evaluation 295 falls to 0.001427206335457971. NF and other final tiny halogen/heteroatom products score near zero, while the heavily expanded seed 0 products can score exactly zero. It does not establish O–F bonding, thiol addition or a particular stereochemistry as a biochemical requirement. Parent best scores by seeds 0/1/2 are 0.35235865253927606, 0.4076078874136615 and 0.19754750998843454; Child values are 0.3681493246147591, 0.4262907971393896 and 0.48914403574662013. transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-51af92d7316d, complete epoch-1 Search seeds 0/1/2, 290 accepted optimizer products per session. Full size tails are 321/4350 below six heavy atoms and 239/4350 above fifty; late counts are 182/2175 and 141/2175. Parent n-b13ef5ae4ba8 has 319/4350 and 244/4350 full, 170/2175 and 141/2175 late. The per-task examples show low scores at both extremes while many better products retain substantial organic frameworks. Evidence and definitions: policy/scratch/r0056-00-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json and policy/scratch/r0056-00-improve-L01/molecular/inputs-sha256.json. This is a chemical association, not a universal size optimum or component attribution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve intermediate-sized complete organic frameworks while exploring: both tiny fragments and oversized products persist late.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs graph edits that preserve coherent molecular size while allowing session feedback to test useful contraction or growth. These observations do not authorize fixed target-specific templates or imply that every large or small molecule should be excluded.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-51af92d7316d, complete epoch-1 Search panel: direct O–halogen bonds occur in 407/4350 products, N–halogen in 167/4350, O–O in 134/4350 and N–O in 713/4350; categories overlap and N–O alone is not an invalidity criterion. The cited higher-score examples include N-fluorinated fused heteroaromatics, acyl fluorides and O-fluorinated cages, so these environments are not confined to poor products. The matched Parent also carries these environments. Original provenance and per-cell counters are in policy/scratch/r0056-00-improve-L01/molecular/inputs-sha256.json and policy/scratch/r0056-00-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json; no stability or synthesis measurement was made.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks a consistently ordinary bond-environment alternative to some of its highly scored heteroatom-rich products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate chemically coherent alternatives to unusual heteroatom bonds and let current-session feedback compare them. Any plausibility constraint should distinguish ordinary N–O functional groups from specific reactive or synthetically difficult environments, rather than treating a graph-valid bond or a high score as proof of makeability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-51af92d7316d under the same complete Search conditions: every task digest has stereocentre-text rate zero, yet RDKit FindMolChiralCenters(includeUnassigned=True) finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2476/4350 optimizer products. The cited basic-amine ring products and densely substituted heteroatom cages visibly exemplify this mismatch. The Parent count is 2566/4350, so the gap is inherited in scope; no score benefit from explicit stereochemistry is established. Methods and source hashes are in policy/scratch/r0056-00-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json and policy/scratch/r0056-00-improve-L01/molecular/inputs-sha256.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator explores stereogenic saturated rings and cages without specifying their stereochemical identities.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A general generator needs to represent and retain stereochemical identity when edits create stereogenic centres, or explicitly treat the output as an unresolved mixture. Whether stereochemical exploration helps an objective must be learned from that session, not inferred from a benchmark identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-51af92d7316d, epoch-1 Search seeds 0/1/2: per-task nonempty typed scaffold counts span 309..445 and generic counts 208..326, yet higher-score examples often share local amine–aryl or heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangements while weak proposals fragment, overgrow or reorganize them. Free basic amines are already produced; claiming that the generator cannot make them would be false. The complete matched Parent preserves both similar successes and similar liabilities. See policy/scratch/r0056-00-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json and its exact trajectory citations. This supports a chemical coverage question, not proof about the selector, tree, edit operator or a transferable preferred scaffold.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad scaffold production does not ensure retention of the useful functional-group arrangements present in the generator’s own stronger products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is feedback-conditioned exploration that can retain useful local functional arrangements while varying their surrounding scaffold. Assess that capability with the current session’s accepted molecules and scores, without importing named objectives, answer structures or cross-session labels.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
